- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/auto-org-admin-grant.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/invitation-placement.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin 6f5d40f4a8837caedc6a9234cbadd56ddb447be9 && git checkout 6f5d40f4a8837caedc6a9234cbadd56ddb447be9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76 20eb5f1f6d24c743c27ab7dcceb52707db7802bd && git checkout -B drift-repro 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76 && git merge --no-ff 20eb5f1f6d24c743c27ab7dcceb52707db7802bd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 · 2026-10-20T03:18Z

`os-justin` · `session_011TdZ8GjixNZFLz1xJD9zzK` (seat post #6021). Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main` `0904d856e3`, not against the report (os-dev-report 6282206380 on #24136). Disclosure read first: the PR body, the changeset and the report state the boundary and its refusals; none gives a recipe against any door. Head under review:

```text
20eb5f1f6d24c743c27ab7dcceb52707db7802bd
```

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #24136`, line-start `Clause-②: no` in the body and the changeset. The body names #20136, #23960, #24164 and #24341 with no keyword beside any of them; the only closing keyword in the body is the first line's. The changeset is `@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor` (ruling item 3), and the package is published (`files[]` in its `package.json`). Each changeset sentence was read against the diff: the three conditions, the by-name exclusions, create-and-remove only, the stamping of an organization-less insert, the 403 / 400 split, `allowCreate` / `allowDelete` true with `allowEdit` false, and the two doors. 13 files, none on a governed surface (`governedPathsIn` answers `[]`). The trial merge onto `origin/main` is clean; `main` moved by #24713 and #24718 since the base, neither in a region this PR edits.
2. **The ruling, measured by the seat.**
   - The three conditions in `organizationBoundaryFailure` are the ADR-0090 D12 note's (a), (b) and (c), read against `docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md:535–600` on `main`. Condition (c) reads the security catalog's `capability` kind, which the catalog serves (`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts:106`). The by-name list is the ADR's: `admin_full_access`, both organization-administrator sets and the three D10 agent ceilings. There is no fourth condition (E′ on #24164, item 9).
   - Holding an organization-administrator set means administering the active organization only: the resolver applies a stored grant when its organization is null or the active one (`grantAppliesInTenant`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:861`), and `auto-org-admin-grant.ts` always writes the grant with the membership's organization.
   - "Tenant-level" moves only for the two organization-administrator sets. Any other wildcard holder keeps today's pass-through, as the dispatch requires. The gate governs exactly `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set` and `sys_member`; on `sys_member` an organization administrator is now refused at the gate, on a path the file itself records as unreachable today.
   - Removing an organization-administrator grant is refused by name, so one administrator cannot demote another; that status still comes from the membership grade alone.
3. **Refusals and pins.** Every refusal case asserts the ADR-0112 envelope as a pair (`[status, code]` equal to `[403, 'PERMISSION_DENIED']` or `[400, 'VALIDATION_FAILED']`) in the real-stack posture file. The gate unit file asserts `code` and `status` through one helper. Six ablations are reported, each red and restored with blob equal to HEAD. Ablation 6 (the walled administrator read as tenant-level again) turns all four boundary files red, so the posture matrix carries load.
4. **Gates.** At ACCEPT, every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate). This includes TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Locally, 70 of 71 derived families exited 0 at this head. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` is NOT MEASURED locally (shallow clone) and is covered by CI's lint lane.
5. **Accepted deviations.** The claim surface is amended to cover three items:
   - `get-effective-object-permissions.test.ts`: the #20136 parity pin follows the ruled overrides (create and delete true, edit false).
   - `__tests__/security-catalog.testkit.ts`: an optional capability list, test infrastructure only.
   - A read-only import of `objects/reserved-identity-names.ts`.

   No other open PR touches these files. `SharingServicePlugin` is not composed in the posture file; the assignment tables carry no sharing.
6. **Done-when residuals.**
   - **#23960's HTTP re-run.** NOT MEASURED through the HTTP door. The real-stack posture file stands in, and the route is unchanged.
   - **Console check.** Measured by the seat with a static read of `objectstack-ai/objectui`; it needs no code. Setup's two holder sections show Add and Remove from the caller's `allowCreate` / `allowDelete` (`resolveAffordance('relatedNew' / 'relatedRowDelete')`) and never read `allowEdit`. The invite dialog shows placement whenever `placeableBusinessUnitIds` and `assignablePositions` are both non-empty, and reads neither `isTenantAdmin` nor `scopes`. The comments, README text and test fixture there that describe the organization administrator as read-only become stale when this lands. The seat files that follow-up in objectui after the merge.
7. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - The delegated walk `setsBoundToPosition` does not count the set of the position's own name, which the resolver grants. Confirmed on `main`: `security-plugin.ts:6578` and `delegated-admin-gate.ts:1086`. Disposition: filed #24736.
   - The tenant-level `my-delegable-scope` offers the ADR-0068 D2 identity positions, which the write path refuses. Disposition: filed #24737.
   - The `plugin-auth` `auth-manager.ts` comment above `beforeCreateInvitation` still argues the read-only premise. Disposition: `Acceptance notes`; the seat records it on its seat post's list of stale code comments.
   - `docs/design/permission-model.md` §10 covers only delegated administration. Disposition: `Acceptance notes`.
8. **Landing clause.** No contract review is owed. The change is a runtime permission change ruled by the maintainer (B on #23960), declared `Clause-②: no` on the ruling's own words. It touches no `packages/spec` text, no governed surface and no published schema. Next step: ready + auto-merge through the relay once every check on the current head is green or an expected skip.
